NAME GRAMMAR: DOOR_<SWING|LIFT|SLIDING_CAVITY|SLIDING_FACE|CP_SLIDE|GEN_SWING>_<leaf count>[_SOLID|_GLASS_FULL|_VISION PANEL_NARROW] - <leaf width>[x<2nd leaf width>]x<height>[_INT], then -<Revit element id>-<view name> (V<n> = virtual copy); '900x2000' = clear leaf width x height, 'AxBxH' = two leaves + height; Curtain Wall Door_Swing and DOOR_CP_SLIDE carry no size; BIM names are Revit door tags (D36, D37, Door NO_03/17). INSERT POINT / ROTATION / MIRROR: local +x = run direction = (cos rot, sin rot); the origin is on the wall axis (within about 0.1 m) and at the centre of the opening for every family EXCEPT D36 and Door NO_03 (unequal double leaves: origin at the meeting stile) and Door-Opening (8 mm off). rot is only 0 / 90 / 180 / -90; no INSERT in either file is mirrored or scaled (0 of 492 / 442), so handing is baked into separate block geometry: read the hinge from the leaf line / arc end; the swing side is local +y for DOOR_*, D37, D_Swing_Single, Door NO_03 and the ARCH door, local -y for D36 and Curtain Wall Door_Swing. ENDS (a, b = origin -/+ half widths along local x; measured wall/glass ends agree to 4 mm): SWING_1 900 +-0.49 (gap 0.98); SWING_1 750 +-0.415 (0.83); GEN_SWING_1 700 +-0.40 (0.80); SWING_2 900 +-0.94 (1.88); LIFT_2 +-0.49 (0.98); CP_SLIDE +-1.00 (2.00; leaves drawn out to +-1.5, with arrows); CAVITY_2 2340 +-0.96 (1.92); CAVITY_2 3100 +-1.24 (2.48); CAVITY_1 +-0.64 (1.28); FACE_2 +-2.40 (4.80); Door-Opening -0.458/+0.442 (0.90); Curtain Wall Door_Swing +-0.45 (0.90) or +-0.50 (1.00, id 4494147) set in glass; BIM: D37 +-0.51 (1.02), D36 -1.06/+0.56 (1.62), Door NO_03 -1.06/+0.46 (1.52), D_Swing_Single 900 -0.514/+0.506 (1.02), 700 -0.414/+0.406 (0.82), Door NO_17 +-0.50 (1.00), D_Openning_Lift +-0.75 (1.50); ARCH double door +-1.00 (2.00). conversionCheck: Compared each DXF with LibreDWG's own dwgread -O JSON dump of the DWG (dwgjson/L29.json, L30.json; scripts s08, s09). Entity counts over all block definitions incl. model space: L29 10,968 = LINE 7281, ARC 1404, SPLINE 755, LWPOLYLINE 558, INSERT 492, HATCH 248, ELLIPSE 192, CIRCLE 38; L30 12,164 = LINE 9011, ARC 1220, LWPOLYLINE 574, SPLINE 503, INSERT 442, HATCH 261, ELLIPSE 121, CIRCLE 32. The DXF has exactly the same count for every (type, layer) pair (0 mismatching groups) and every (block, type) pair; e.g. A-WALL (L29) LINE 1191 / HATCH 119 / SPLINE 8 / ARC 6 / LWPOLYLINE 4; A-DOOR LINE 275 / ARC 34 / CIRCLE 6 / INSERT 17; A-GLAZ-CURT LINE 2444 / HATCH 25 / INSERT 12; S-COLS HATCH 17 / LINE 112; L30 A-WALL LINE 1418 / HATCH 106 / INSERT 1, A-DOOR LINE 172 / ARC 35 / HATCH 1 / INSERT 14. No TEXT, MTEXT, DIMENSION, ATTRIB, SOLID, 3DFACE, MLEADER or unknown entities exist in either DWG. 'Skip HATCH common handles due to short handle stream' appears 248 / 261 times = once per HATCH (every hatch, not a subset), plus class warnings for MATERIAL / TABLESTYLE / MLEADERSTYLE (non-geometry; one 'Unhandled Object TABLESTYLE in out_dxf'). Nothing that matters is lost: all 248 / 261 hatches are in the DXF with the same handle, block owner, layer, pattern (SOLID or FP_n), solid flag and all 371 / 386 boundary loops with identical edge counts. Independent plausibility test (the JSON and DXF share one parser): A-WALL hatch loops lie on A-WALL lines for a median 98% of their length (placebo vs A-GLAZ-CURT lines 0%), S-COLS 100%, A-GLAZ-CURT 100%, A-GENM 100%, Q-CASE 100%, S-STRS 87-93%, A-WALL-PATT on A-WALL/S-COLS lines 92-96%, so layers were not scrambled. The skipped handles (owner/reactors/linetype/material-type data) are unused by the pipeline. The Revit XDATA survives in the DXF. Limits: no second DWG reader was available, so a silently undecoded object would be missing from both outputs (HANDSEED 14178 vs 11,816 objects read).
heights: No heights are stored: every entity has z=0, thickness 0, extrusion (0,0,1); there is no TEXT / MTEXT / DIMENSION / ATTRIB (so no ceiling heights, level marks, spot elevations, room names or door tags); level names exist only in the view names ('LEVEL 29 DIMENSION PLAN', 'Level 30 Rev - Option 1_3 - BANQUET') and the link name 'Level L01 - ROOF'. Heights occur only in block names. Door heights: SWING_1 / SWING_2 900x2000 and 750x2000, Door-Opening 900 x 2000, BIM D_Swing_Single 900x2000 / 700_2000 and Shaft_1000_2000 = 2.00 m; DOOR_LIFT_2_SOLID 900x2100 = 2.10; D_Openning_Lift 1400 X 2250mm = 2.25; CAVITY_1 920x2340 and CAVITY_2 920x920x2340 = 2.34; DOOR_GEN_SWING_1 PANEL_FLUSH 700x2400 and DOOR_SLIDING_FACE_2 2400x2400x2400 = 2.40; DOOR_SLIDING_CAVITY_2_SOLID 920x920x3100 = 3.10 (L30 only). No height in D36, D37, Door NO_03, Curtain Wall Door_Swing, CP_SLIDE ('GLASS_FULL' = full height) or the ARCH double door; the facade is full-height curtain wall with no sill/head data. Furniture heights in names: desks 780H, CENTER_TABLE R250 400H, LOCKER_SINGLE_3 HIGH. Floor-to-floor is not stored (see floorToFloor).
floorToFloorReasoning: Inconclusive, so 4.20 m. There is no level, elevation or ceiling information (z=0, no text). Stair evidence: both stairs (BIM link, identical on L29 and L30) are two-flight half-landing stairs that climb one storey. West stair: 2 flights x 7 treads at 0.25 m going (left flight riser lines y=-47.316..-45.566, right flight -47.566..-45.816; 7 FP_6 + 7 FP_5 tread hatches on L30) = 16 risers. East stair: 2 flights x 9 treads at 0.28 m going (x 8.417..10.938 north, 8.698..11.217 south; 9 + 9 FP_2 hatches on L30) = 20 risers. With 0.175 m (top of the normal 0.15-0.175 range; 175 / 280 is a clean 7 in / 11 in design) the east stair gives 3.50 m and the west 2.80 m; with 0.15 m 3.00 and 2.40 m. Two stairs in one core cannot have different rises, so the riser counts contradict each other (west would need 0.22 m risers at 3.5 m, east 0.21 m at 4.2 m), and both results are too low for the other evidence: L30 has a 3.10 m high door (DOOR_SLIDING_CAVITY_2_SOLID 920x920x3100) and 2.34-2.40 m sliders, which do not fit a 2.8-3.5 m storey once slab and ceiling void are added; tower office floors are normally 4.0-4.5 m. The zig-zag cut-mark positions do not yield a consistent riser height either. 4.20 m would imply 24 risers at 0.175 m, which neither stair as drawn has. Risk: if the true value is the east stair's 3.50 m, walls built at 4.20 m are 20% too tall.
surprises: Door data is split over three sources: only the model-space doors (17 / 14) are A-DOOR INSERTs; 8 BIM doors + 1 ARCH double door per floor are nested blocks on layer 0 inside the links (found only by name or by walking nested INSERTs). Their leaf outline lives on A-DETL-GENF and the swing arc on A-DETL-GENF-HDLN, while A-DOOR holds only jamb sections, dashed head lines and 24 arcs of 5 mm radius that look like swings but are round ends.

The insert point is not always the opening centre (D36 and Door NO_03 unequal leaves, Door-Opening 8 mm off) and drawn geometry overshoots the opening (open leaves, slider leaves, pockets, arrows), so bbox-based widths are wrong: DOOR_SWING_2 id 4484608 bbox 3.49 m for a 1.88 m gap, CP_SLIDE 3.0 m for 2.0 m.

Cavity sliders cut a pocket slot (a hole in the wall fill) beside the frame: a wall-end search along the wall axis returns +1.80 m (CAVITY_1) and +-2.40 m (the 3100 slider) instead of the frame faces +0.64 / +-1.24; the wall is continuous around the pocket.
Names mislead for two sliders (920 vs 1.20 m clear; 920x920x3100 vs 2.40 m clear) and carry no size at all for Curtain Wall Door_Swing (0.90 or 1.00) and DOOR_CP_SLIDE (2.00).

Lifts: door blocks only on L29 (0.98 m gaps); on L30 the same shaft wall has 1.40 m gaps with no leaf. The lift-car box with X is on A-DOOR-FRAM inside the L29 door blocks (18 lines each) and on A-DETL elsewhere, so A-DOOR-FRAM length is not all frame.

A-WALL is not only walls: ARCH-link A-WALL is facade fins and caps (518 / 714 lines, 78% / 74% shorter than 0.2 m, plus splines, ellipses, arcs); BIM walls are composite strips (0.01 skins) so hatch widths read 0.07 for 0.10-0.20 m walls; glass lobby screens are 0.01-0.02 m A-WALL hatches; every wall is 4+ separate LINEs plus 1-2 hatches (A-WALL + A-WALL-PATT duplicate the fill).

A-DETL-GENF carries a SOLID hatch with 37 / 31 loops (about 160 m2 net room fill over the core) that looks like wall poche. On L30 only, 12 thin A-DETL lines run across wall openings (door gaps 0.80, 0.82, 1.00, 1.02 x3, 1.52, 1.62; stair entrance 1.20; north stair gap 1.75) and also close two open room sides (1.95 m at x=2.52, y -37.74..-35.79; 0.60 m at y=-41.06): wall-like lines through openings that are not on a wall layer.

Link walls change per floor: the east stair's north ROOF wall has its 1.75 m gap at x 11.27-13.02 on L29 (spanned by a 0.1 m model-space strip) but at x 6.77-8.52 on L30; BIM has 14 extra wall lines on L30; ROOF columns 8 vs 5. Coordinates are identical but link content is not a copy.

Glass uses four mechanisms: about 5,000 tiny A-GLAZ-CURT primitives per floor (facade, including WT-05-balustrade screens up to 10 m long that look like glass partitions), 'System Panel - GLAZED' blocks (10 mm-thick rectangles, L29 only), 0.01-0.02 m A-WALL hatches (lobby screens) and the ARCH double door; door gaps in glass equal the leaf width; there are no windows, sills or window layers at all.
No TEXT, MTEXT, DIMENSION or ATTRIB anywhere (the 'dimension plan' contains no dimensions): no room names, tags or levels; z=0, units mm. Every role must come from layers, block names and geometry.

Revit XDATA (appid REVIT, strings '<elementId>_<categoryId>': -2000011 walls, -2000170 curtain panels, -2001330 structural columns, -2000120 stairs, -2000032 floors) survives in the DXF but only on link geometry, and the nested INSERTs of the BIM link are mis-tagged (all 46 = Doors -2000023 on L29, all 46 = structural columns on L30), so category ids cannot separate doors from columns; no window category (-2000014) occurs. prims.py does not read XDATA.

No mirrored or scaled INSERTs (0 of 492 / 442) and rotations are only 0 / 90 / 180 / -90 for doors: handing is in the block geometry; one block can serve several instances (3 lift doors, 2 DOOR_SWING_2 on L30), and the INSERT item 'h' handle of everything inside a link is the link's handle.

L29 A-FLOR along the south facade (y=-59.05) is 26 segments with 25 gaps (23 x 0.09 m): it looks like a wall line full of openings but is the slab edge; A-AREA lines (L29) run 5 cm beside the glass partitions and across their door gaps.

Doorless openings exist without any door block: west stair entrance 1.20 m (both floors), east stair gaps 1.75 m (position differs per floor); the same WC wall opening is a Door-Opening (0.90) on L29 but a flush door block (0.80) on L30, so a door cannot be carried from one floor to the other.

The two stairs disagree on risers per storey (16 vs 20), so they cannot fix the floor height; L30's plate ends about 3 m north of L29's on the south side (south facade and SE glazed room differ) although origin, core and facade lines coincide.
